paragraphs: A treatment can change outcomes even when it leaves their average unchanged. For example, it might make outcomes more variable or more consistent. This paper addresses that broader question: whether a binary treatment changes the distribution of outcomes, rather than only their mean. That target captures effects that an average treatment effect alone would miss.

The authors propose a kernel-based statistical test for these distributional effects. The test is doubly robust and comes with a proof of valid type-I error control. In practical terms, the error-control result concerns the risk of declaring a treatment effect when the relevant null hypothesis is true. This makes statistical reliability a central part of the contribution.

The algorithm also avoids permutations, removing the need for that computational procedure when carrying out the test. The authors describe it, to their knowledge, as the first kernel-based doubly robust test with proven type-I error validity. Its contribution combines a broader target for causal analysis with a computationally efficient testing method.
neurips-2023-an-efficient-doubly-robust-.tldr: The paper introduces an efficient, doubly robust kernel test for treatment effects on outcome distributions, with proven type-I error control.

paragraphs: Android in the Wild (AitW) is a dataset for studying systems that follow written instructions by operating an Android device’s interface. It pairs human demonstrations with the instructions they carry out, recording both screens and actions. Its 715,000 episodes cover 30,000 distinct instructions, providing examples of how language connects to sequences of device interactions.

The tasks require understanding both the instruction’s meaning and the visual context across multiple steps. A system must infer possible interactions from what appears on screen and produce precise gestures. For example, operating a carousel can require a horizontal scroll. This makes choosing an action a problem of interpreting appearance and controlling movement, beyond simply selecting an interface element.

The demonstrations span four Android versions and eight device types with different screen resolutions. The dataset is organized to support analysis of performance on unfamiliar task descriptions, applications, or platform versions. The authors also develop two agents and report their performance across the dataset. Together, the demonstrations and evaluations provide a basis for investigating how device-control systems handle these variations; the abstract does not claim that robustness has been solved.
neurips-2023-androidinthewild-a-large-sc.tldr: Android in the Wild provides large-scale human demonstrations for studying how agents follow language instructions through visual interpretation and precise Android interface gestures.

paragraphs: Normalizing flows can generate samples while providing exact likelihoods, a useful combination for modeling physical systems. Those likelihoods allow samples to be reweighted against known energy functions and support unbiased observable estimates. For many-particle systems, effective models also need to respect physical symmetries. Continuous normalizing flows can incorporate these symmetries, but their computational cost has restricted their use.

The paper introduces equivariant flow matching, a training objective based on optimal transport flow matching. It uses symmetries of the target energy to train equivariant continuous flows without simulation during training. The contribution changes how these models are trained while retaining the symmetry-aware modeling approach that makes them suitable for physical distributions.

Experiments cover rotation- and permutation-invariant particle systems and the molecule alanine dipeptide. The authors report shorter integration paths, better sampling efficiency, and greater scalability than existing methods. For alanine dipeptide, they obtain a Boltzmann generator with significant sampling efficiency without tailored internal-coordinate features, showing that this specialized representation was unnecessary for their demonstrated result.
neurips-2023-equivariant-flow-matching-a.tldr: Equivariant flow matching uses physical symmetries for simulation-free training of continuous normalizing flows, improving sampling efficiency in the studied systems.

paragraphs: Long sequences make causal self-attention expensive because its computation grows quadratically with sequence length. Sparse attention reduces the connections being computed, but fewer connections do not automatically mean faster execution. The authors highlight that dynamic sparse implementations can run substantially slower than full attention implemented with FlashAttention, while simpler implementations often require fixed attention patterns.

This paper extends FlashAttention to support a broad class of sparse patterns, including approaches that drop keys or queries and approaches based on hashing. The aim is to make flexible sparsity compatible with efficient execution. The authors report implementations without computational-complexity overhead and with multi-fold runtime improvements over FlashAttention.

The gains become visible at longer sequence lengths even with relatively modest sparsity. In the reported language-model training experiments, speed increases by 2.0 times for 8,000-token sequences and 3.3 times for 16,000-token sequences without sacrificing perplexity. These results show that dynamic sparsity can deliver practical training gains when paired with an implementation designed to exploit it.
neurips-2023-fast-attention-over-long-se.tldr: Extending FlashAttention to dynamic sparse patterns accelerates the reported long-sequence language-model training without sacrificing perplexity.

paragraphs: A pretrained vision transformer may represent images well while attending to the wrong entities for a particular classification task. This matters when only a few labeled examples are available: objects unrelated to the target classes can distract the model even after fine-tuning. The paper aims to make adaptation explicitly guide attention toward the entities that distinguish the current classes.

The method first combines attention information with gradients to locate important entities in the labeled support images. These locations become position prompts. It then uses a cross-entropy objective between a many-hot representation of the selected positions and the model’s attention logits. This supplies a direct training signal about where the model should focus.

The learned focus can carry over to query images that were not used as support examples. Experiments show improvements for both full fine-tuning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning on few-shot tasks. The method also applies across different transformer structures and both single-modality and vision-language pretraining, making attention guidance usable in several adaptation settings.
neurips-2023-focus-your-attention-when-f.tldr: Automatically locating class-relevant entities and supervising attention improves vision-transformer fine-tuning for few-shot image classification.

paragraphs: Language models contain broad semantic knowledge, but that knowledge alone does not tell a robot what it can physically accomplish. Such models may lack access to non-language observations and the rewards or constraints relevant to action. Policies trained through interaction offer physical grounding, yet their more limited training data can leave them short of high-level semantic understanding.

Grounded Decoding combines these complementary sources of knowledge while constructing an action sequence. It seeks sequences that receive high probability from the language model and also satisfy probabilistic objectives supplied by grounded models. The authors frame this process as similar to probabilistic filtering: generation is guided jointly by linguistic plausibility and models of what the environment supports.

The paper demonstrates how to obtain grounded models across three simulation and real-world domains. Its decoding strategy solves complex, long-horizon embodied tasks in the reported robotic settings. The result supports using environmental knowledge during sequence generation, so the language model’s semantic knowledge contributes to plans that grounded models also judge realizable.
neurips-2023-grounded-decoding-guiding-t.tldr: Grounded Decoding combines language-model probabilities with environment-grounded objectives to generate realizable action sequences for embodied tasks.

paragraphs: Federated reinforcement learning lets agents train a shared policy while keeping their individual experience data local. Communication can nevertheless become expensive, especially for natural policy gradient methods, which use second-order information. This paper targets the amount of information agents must exchange to coordinate those updates without giving up the convergence behavior of the standard federated method.

The proposed FedNPG-ADMM framework uses the alternating direction method of multipliers to approximate the global natural policy gradient direction. The authors prove that communication per iteration scales linearly with the number of model parameters instead of quadratically. That change addresses how communication costs grow as the policy model becomes larger.

Their analysis retains the standard FedNPG iteration rate for reaching an epsilon-error stationary point: order 1 divided by the product of epsilon and the squared quantity one minus the discount factor. In MuJoCo experiments, the method maintains standard FedNPG’s reward performance. The evaluations also show improved convergence as the number of participating federated agents increases.
neurips-2023-improved-communication-effi.tldr: FedNPG-ADMM reduces per-iteration communication from quadratic to linear in model size while preserving the stated convergence rate of federated natural policy gradient.

paragraphs: Controlling a physically simulated character through natural language requires connecting rich instructions with motions that a physical environment can support. A motion plan may express the requested behavior yet contain invalid states or transitions the character cannot execute. InsActor addresses both the interpretation of instructions and the conversion of planned motion into physically simulated behavior.

The framework uses diffusion policies for motion planning with flexible conditioning. These policies capture relationships between high-level instructions and character movement. To handle infeasible planned transitions, InsActor discovers low-level skills and maps motion plans into sequences of those skills in a compact latent space. This gives the framework a way to translate high-level plans into lower-level behavior.

The authors report state-of-the-art results on several tasks, including instruction-driven motion generation and instruction-driven waypoint heading. The experiments support the framework’s ability to produce simulated animations from high-level language. The authors particularly emphasize its usefulness for long-horizon tasks involving varied instructions, where connecting successive planned motions to executable skills is central.
neurips-2023-insactor-instruction-driven.tldr: InsActor combines diffusion-based motion planning with learned low-level skills to animate physics-based characters from high-level instructions.

paragraphs: Transforming visual observations during training can help reinforcement learning agents learn from fewer interactions. This paper investigates which properties make those transformations effective. Its experiments identify a useful combination for individual operations: substantial spatial diversity alongside only slight difficulty added to the learning problem. The authors use that finding to design Random PadResize, an augmentation offering varied spatial arrangements with minimal hardness.

The paper also examines why combining several augmentation types can fail to outperform individual operations. In the studied fusion schemes, combinations introduce greater difficulty and unstable data distributions. This is particularly relevant to reinforcement learning, where the learning process is already non-stationary and the observations available to the agent change over time.

Cycling Augmentation addresses that issue by rotating periodically through different augmentation operations. It aims to increase the variety of transformation types while keeping the data distribution consistent. Evaluations on the DeepMind Control suite and CARLA driving simulator show that the proposed methods achieve better sample efficiency than the prior state-of-the-art methods considered.
neurips-2023-learning-better-with-less-e.tldr: Random PadResize and Cycling Augmentation improve visual reinforcement learning’s sample efficiency by balancing transformation diversity, difficulty, and distribution consistency.

paragraphs: Soft labels contain a teacher model’s graded predictions rather than a single class choice. Their usefulness is often explained by assuming they closely match ground-truth labels. This paper asks whether they can still teach effectively when that discrepancy is large. The central distinction is between a teacher’s accuracy and the learning value of the soft labels it produces.

The authors introduce two indicators for measuring that value. Using these indicators, they give sufficient conditions under which learning from biased soft labels is classifier-consistent and learnable through empirical risk minimization. These conditions can apply even when label bias is large, extending the theoretical account beyond soft labels that closely approximate the truth.

A heuristic training method produces teachers with below 30% accuracy whose students exceed 90% accuracy on CIFAR-10, comparable to models trained on the original data. The indicators measure the effectiveness of labels in this process. The framework also extends to incomplete supervision, partial labels, and additive noise, with experiments supporting the indicators across these settings.
neurips-2023-learning-from-biased-soft-l.tldr: Biased soft labels can remain effective teaching signals under stated conditions, even when the teacher’s own classification accuracy is very low.

paragraphs: Learning a policy from visual demonstrations is appealing because the demonstrations need not include recorded actions or rewards. The challenge is turning what an agent sees into a useful learning signal. The paper addresses approaches that rely on inefficient online learning or additional task-specific information such as goal states, which can make them unsuitable for open-ended tasks.

Its two-stage framework first pretrains a State-to-Go Transformer offline. The transformer learns to predict and distinguish transitions in the latent representations of demonstrations. In the second stage, it supplies intrinsic rewards for a reinforcement learning agent. The downstream agent learns solely from those intrinsic rewards, connecting visual demonstration structure to action learning.

Experiments on Atari and Minecraft show better performance than the evaluated baselines. On some tasks, performance is comparable to policies trained with environmental rewards. These findings suggest that video-only demonstrations can support difficult visual control tasks without requiring complete offline records of states, actions, and rewards. The comparable-performance result applies to some tasks rather than the entire evaluation.
neurips-2023-learning-from-visual-observ.tldr: An offline-pretrained State-to-Go Transformer turns visual demonstrations into intrinsic rewards that support downstream reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Mixed integer linear programming solvers use cutting planes to improve bounds on the best possible solution. Different separator routines generate different cuts, and modern solvers invoke these routines repeatedly. This paper studies which separators to activate, arguing that managing the generators of cuts can substantially affect solving time.

Choosing a subset of separators creates a combinatorial search space, which makes direct learning difficult. The authors first use a data-driven strategy to restrict that space, then apply a learning-guided algorithm within it. The resulting configurations depend on the problem instance and can change as the solve progresses, allowing separator choices to adapt during computation.

In experiments with the open-source SCIP solver, the method improves relative solve time by up to 72% on synthetic benchmarks and 37% on real-world benchmarks. These are reported upper improvements across the evaluated settings. The contribution complements methods that select individual cutting planes: it shows that decisions about which separator routines run also offer an effective point for learned solver control.
neurips-2023-learning-to-configure-separ.tldr: Learning instance-aware separator configurations accelerates SCIP, with reported relative solve-time improvements up to 72% on synthetic and 37% on real-world benchmarks.

paragraphs: Learning separate representations for objects could make image-based learning more interpretable, robust, and efficient. Many existing approaches learn by reconstructing the input image, but the authors describe difficulties scaling those methods to real-world scenes even with larger models. This paper develops a method that uses feature connectivity to help identify which neighboring pixels belong together.

The method clusters nearby pixels that are likely to represent the same object. It also introduces two object-centric regularization terms that refine the representations in latent space. Together, connectivity-based grouping and these additional training constraints enable the approach to handle complex real-world imagery, addressing the scaling problem identified for earlier reconstruction-oriented methods.

Experiments span simulated images, real-world images, complex textures, and common objects. The authors report substantially better discovered-object quality than state-of-the-art methods, alongside evidence of sample efficiency and generalization. They also show that the learned representations accurately predict key object properties in downstream tasks. This connects the quality of object discovery to the usefulness of the resulting representations.
neurips-2023-multi-object-representation.tldr: Feature-based pixel grouping and object-centric regularization improve object discovery and produce useful representations for complex real-world images.

paragraphs: Text-to-image models offer a convenient way to describe a desired picture, but language alone can be awkward for nuanced ideas. MultiFusion broadens the input interface so users can interleave multiple modalities and languages in a single request. The aim is to let different forms of input work together when specifying what an image should express.

The system brings together pretrained models and aligns them into a cohesive whole. This avoids the need for extensive training from scratch and makes existing model capabilities available to the combined system. The technical emphasis is on integration: separately acquired abilities must become usable by the image generation component.

The experiments show efficient transfer of capabilities from the individual modules to the downstream model. In particular, the combined system enables an image generation module to use multilingual, interleaved multimodal inputs even though that module was trained only on monomodal data in one language. The finding demonstrates that the input capabilities of the assembled system can exceed those directly taught to its image generator.
neurips-2023-multifusion-fusing-pre-trai.tldr: MultiFusion aligns pretrained models so an image generator can respond to interleaved multilingual and multimodal inputs.

paragraphs: Phone and tablet versions of an application often share functionality and much of their interface design. Nevertheless, developers may rebuild tablet interfaces from scratch, increasing effort and leaving existing design work underused. Research on automating this process needs examples of corresponding interfaces across devices, rather than collections containing only phone screens.

The paper introduces Papt, a dataset of paired Android phone and tablet graphical interfaces. It contains 10,035 page pairs drawn from 5,593 distinct application pairs. Pairing is the central contribution: each example connects the two device-specific interfaces, providing data for studying their relationship. The authors also propose new approaches for collecting these paired pages.

The work describes advantages over existing interface datasets and uses preliminary experiments to examine challenges in deep-learning-based interface development. Its main result is a research resource and a collection methodology, alongside an initial investigation of the automation problem. This gives researchers paired evidence for studying interface reuse across phones and tablets, an area the authors identify as lacking publicly available datasets.
neurips-2023-pairwise-gui-dataset-constr.tldr: Papt provides paired Android phone and tablet interface pages to support research on automated cross-device interface development.

paragraphs: Neural-network training is usually presented as a difficult optimization problem, but some formulations can contain hidden convex structure. This paper studies deep parallel ReLU networks, an architectural family that includes standard deep networks and ResNets as special cases. It asks what becomes visible when their training objectives include pathwise regularization.

The authors show that these regularized training problems have exact convex optimization representations. They further prove that the equivalent convex problem uses a norm that encourages group sparsity. This provides an interpretation of the network as a parsimonious high-dimensional convex model, connecting a neural training formulation to a structured preference for fewer active groups.

An exact convex representation does not by itself make the original training problem polynomial-time solvable. The paper therefore proposes an approximate algorithm whose complexity is fully polynomial in all data dimensions and proves strong global optimality guarantees for it. Experiments corroborate the theory. The contribution combines a structural explanation of regularized training with an algorithm designed to address its computational difficulty.
neurips-2023-path-regularization-a-conve.tldr: Pathwise regularization reveals exact convex, group-sparse formulations of parallel ReLU network training and supports an approximate algorithm with global optimality guarantees.

paragraphs: Some reinforcement learning applications begin with recorded experience but also allow additional interaction to improve a policy. Collecting that extra experience can create engineering costs if the system repeatedly switches its exploration policy. This paper studies the option of choosing a single non-reactive exploration policy using the data already available.

The authors propose an algorithm with provable guarantees for designing that exploration policy from an offline dataset. The existing experience therefore informs how further data should be gathered. This connects policy improvement with experimental design: the method uses prior observations to guide an additional collection phase while respecting the preference for one exploration policy.

The theoretical analysis expresses final policy quality in terms of two quantities: the local coverage of the original dataset and the amount of new data collected. This makes the starting dataset’s coverage an explicit part of the guarantee, rather than treating all offline datasets as equally informative. The result provides a formal account of policy improvement under this constrained data-collection arrangement.
neurips-2023-policy-finetuning-in-reinfo.tldr: The paper uses offline experience to design one non-reactive exploration policy, with policy-quality guarantees tied to initial coverage and additional data.

paragraphs: Policy gradient methods train reinforcement learning policies efficiently, but standard versions do not account for uncertainty in how actions lead to subsequent states. Robust policy learning addresses that uncertainty, often with extra optimization costs. This paper introduces robust policy gradient for rectangular robust Markov decision processes, targeting efficient training within that specified problem class.

The derivation supplies a closed-form expression for the worst occupation measure, which describes visitation under the worst-case dynamics. It also reveals that the worst transition kernel is a rank-one perturbation of the nominal kernel. Combining the occupation measure with robust Q-value estimation produces an explicit expression for the robust policy gradient.

The resulting gradient can be estimated from data with the same time complexity as its non-robust counterpart. This reduces the computational burden associated with the convex optimization problems used by existing robust policy gradient approaches. The result makes uncertainty-aware updates more computationally accessible for rectangular robust MDPs, rather than establishing such a conclusion for every possible model of transition uncertainty.
neurips-2023-policy-gradient-for-rectang.tldr: Robust policy gradient exploits closed-form worst-case structure to match non-robust gradient estimation’s time complexity for rectangular robust MDPs.

paragraphs: The binding problem asks how a fixed network can represent objects and connect the information belonging to each one. Many unsupervised machine learning approaches use discrete object slots, which the authors argue can restrict representation and make uncertainty difficult to express. Continuous, distributed object representations offer another direction, but an earlier complex-valued autoencoder approach worked only on simple toy data.

Rotating Features extends complex-valued features into higher-dimensional representations. The paper also introduces an evaluation procedure for extracting objects from distributed representations. These contributions address both how object information is represented and how researchers can recover objects from that information to evaluate what the model has learned.

The authors additionally demonstrate that the approach applies to pretrained features. Together, these developments allow distributed object-centric representations to scale from toy examples to real-world data. The result establishes broader applicability for this representation strategy. The authors view it as a promising direction for the binding problem in machine learning, with further innovation remaining a possibility rather than an established outcome.
neurips-2023-rotating-features-for-objec.tldr: Rotating Features generalizes complex-valued object representations to higher dimensions and extends distributed object discovery to real-world data.

paragraphs: Agents learning separately may encounter experiences that would help one another. Sharing everything, however, is not the only way to benefit from that information. This paper introduces Selective Multi-Agent Prioritized Experience Relay, in which agents pass along a limited number of observed training transitions. Its guiding idea is that a small set of relevant experiences can improve another agent’s learning.

The approach supports largely decentralized training and requires only a limited communication channel between agents. Experience selection is therefore central to both the communication arrangement and the learning method. Each agent can benefit from observations gathered elsewhere without making unrestricted exchange of all experience the basis of training.

The reported experiments outperform both decentralized training without sharing and state-of-the-art multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms. Selectively sharing a small number of highly relevant transitions also performs better than sharing every experience. The gains persist across a range of hyperparameters and DQN variants, supporting the usefulness of selective exchange across the tested configurations rather than only one narrowly chosen setup.
neurips-2023-selectively-sharing-experie.tldr: Sharing a small set of relevant experiences improves the reported multi-agent learning results, outperforming both no sharing and sharing all experiences.

paragraphs: Landsat has accumulated more than fifty years of multispectral Earth imagery, but small labeled datasets and a lack of foundation models have limited deep-learning adoption for its analysis. SSL4EO-L addresses these resource gaps with a dataset designed for self-supervised learning. It contains five million image patches covering three sensors and two product levels in the Landsat family.

The work also updates and re-releases the L7 Irish and L8 Biome cloud-detection datasets. It introduces machine learning benchmarks for Landsats 4–5 TM and Landsat 7 ETM+ SR. These contributions provide both pretraining material and task-specific evaluation resources, supporting the development and assessment of models across additional Landsat imagery.

Using SSL4EO-L, the authors pretrain foundation models and evaluate them on multiple semantic segmentation tasks. All datasets and model weights are made available through TorchGeo. The contribution is a coordinated set of data, benchmarks, and pretrained models that makes Landsat-focused experimentation more accessible. The abstract reports these evaluations without asserting a particular numerical improvement over previous analysis methods.
neurips-2023-ssl4eo-l-datasets-and-found.tldr: SSL4EO-L provides five million Landsat patches, updated benchmarks, and pretrained foundation models for Earth-observation research.

paragraphs: Particle-based generative models transform sample distributions through differential equations. Generative adversarial networks are commonly described differently, through training a generator network that maps inputs into generated samples. This paper questions that separation and develops a framework connecting the two views. The goal is to understand their relationship at the level of the generative process.

The framework treats generator training as a generalization of particle models. Under this interpretation, a generator network becomes an optional component of such a model rather than the defining boundary between particle-based and adversarial generation. This opens up combinations that are less natural when the two model families are treated as fundamentally separate.

Two constructions follow from the framework: adding a generator to a score-based diffusion model and training a GAN without a generator. The authors test their viability empirically as proofs of concept. These experiments support the possibility of the proposed combinations; their stated role is to illustrate potential applications of the unifying framework, rather than establish universal performance superiority.
neurips-2023-unifying-gans-and-score-bas.tldr: A shared particle-model framework connects GANs and score-based diffusion, motivating diffusion with a generator and adversarial generation without one.

paragraphs: Strong language performance does not by itself establish how useful a model is for chemistry. This paper builds an eight-task benchmark to examine that question across understanding, reasoning, and explaining. Its purpose is to map capabilities across chemistry tasks, using recognized datasets, rather than develop a new method aimed at achieving the highest benchmark score.

The study evaluates GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Davinci-003, Llama, and Galactica on each task. It examines zero-shot prompting and few-shot in-context learning, using specially designed prompts and selected demonstration examples. This makes the prompting setting part of the evaluation, alongside the identity of the model being tested.

GPT-4 outperforms the other evaluated models, while the models show different levels of competitiveness across the eight tasks. The analysis also examines limitations and how in-context learning settings affect performance. These findings support evaluating chemistry capability task by task: the benchmark reveals variation that a single broad statement about a model’s scientific ability would obscure.
neurips-2023-what-can-large-language-mod.tldr: An eight-task chemistry benchmark compares five language models and finds GPT-4 strongest overall, with capabilities varying across tasks and prompting settings.

paragraphs: A goal-conditioned policy maps the current state and a desired goal to the next action. Representing that mapping as a feed-forward neural network raises a structural question: how large or deep must the network become as planning problems grow? This paper studies that question for relational networks, including graph neural networks and transformers.

The authors connect neural policy representations to serialized goal regression search. They use this connection to analyze circuit complexity, focusing on how network width and depth grow with the number of objects and the planning horizon. Their analysis identifies three general classes of planning problems and supplies constructive proofs, showing how the relevant representations can be built.

The work also illustrates how this analysis can guide network design for policy learning. Its significance is that planning structure can inform architectural requirements rather than leaving network size entirely to trial and error. The stated results concern representation and circuit scaling; they provide a way to reason about neural policies without asserting that every representable policy will be easy to learn.
neurips-2023-what-planning-problems-can-.tldr: A circuit-complexity analysis classifies planning problems by how relational neural policy width and depth scale with objects and planning horizon.

paragraphs: Computing Nash equilibria in general multiplayer Markov games is computationally difficult. This paper asks whether a structured class of games can avoid that obstacle. Inspired by zero-sum polymatrix normal-form games, the authors define multi-agent Markov games with pairwise interactions organized by a graph that may change from one state to another.

For this zero-sum class, they show that an epsilon-approximate Nash equilibrium can be computed efficiently. The central theoretical step is an equilibrium-collapse result: the set of coarse-correlated equilibria collapses to the set of Nash equilibria. This connects an equilibrium concept supported by existing computational methods to the Nash equilibrium sought by the paper.

As a consequence, algorithms that compute approximate coarse-correlated equilibria in Markovian policies can be used to obtain approximate Nash equilibria for this class. The result identifies a tractable setting within a generally hard problem. Its scope depends on the specified zero-sum, pairwise interaction structure; it does not remove the computational difficulty for unrestricted multiplayer Markov games.
neurips-2023-zero-sum-polymatrix-markov-.tldr: For a structured class of zero-sum multiplayer Markov games, equilibrium collapse enables efficient computation of approximate Nash equilibria.
